title: France's cultural recovery returned to pre-pandemic levels while education, income, age, and place still stratify access
source_unit: France Ministry of Culture DEPS and CREDOC Conditions de vie et aspirations cultural outings barometer 2024
geography: France; population aged 15 years and above

observations.period: 2024 cultural-outings barometer; previous 12 months, compared with 2019 and 2023

denominator.unit: online survey respondents aged 15 years and above living in France

cinema_2024.unit: percent going to the cinema in the previous 12 months

cinema_2019.unit: percent going to the cinema in the previous 12 months

live_performance_2024.unit: percent attending a professional live performance in the previous 12 months

live_performance_2019.unit: percent attending a professional live performance in the previous 12 months

library_2024.unit: percent visiting a library or media library in the previous 12 months

monument_2024.unit: percent visiting a monument in the previous 12 months

mechanism.value: Aggregate cultural outings recovered to approximately pre-pandemic levels across cinema and live performance, with libraries reaching their highest reported rate in the available comparison series

observations.method: CREDOC Conditions de vie et aspirations survey module commissioned by the Ministry of Culture; online administration to 3,000 people aged 15 and above, with 2024 results based on the January 2025 wave and comparisons to earlier waves.
observations.uncertainty: These are retrospective self-reports in a repeated survey module; the comparison does not identify causal recovery drivers, spending, frequency distribution beyond selected measures, or whether all population groups recovered equally.
observations.subgroup: Population aged 15 years and above in France.
observations.counterinterpretation: Headline return to 2019 rates can mask compositional change, one-time attendance, different intensity, and persistent exclusion among lower-access groups.

observations.period: 2024 cultural-outings barometer; age, education, and gender gradients

denominator.unit: online survey respondents aged 15 years and above living in France

cinema_age_15_24.unit: percent of 15-24 year-olds going to the cinema

cinema_age_70_plus.unit: percent of people aged 70 and above going to the cinema

museum_under_bac.unit: percent of people below the baccalaureate visiting a museum or exhibition

museum_bac_plus_3.unit: percent of people with at least three years of higher education visiting a museum or exhibition

library_age_15_24.unit: percent of 15-24 year-olds visiting a library or media library

library_age_70_plus.unit: percent of people aged 70 and above visiting a library or media library

mechanism.value: Cultural recovery is strongly life-course- and education-stratified; the aggregate return to pre-pandemic levels does not imply equal access or equal cultural optionality

observations.method: Descriptive cross-tabulations from the 2024 CREDOC cultural-outings module, using age and educational-attainment groups.
observations.uncertainty: The cross-tabs do not establish whether education, age, income, school exposure, location, health, transport, or cultural preference drives the observed differences; some youth attendance may be school-related.
observations.subgroup: Age groups and education groups among people aged 15 years and above in France.
observations.counterinterpretation: The age gradient may partly reflect life-cycle, schooling, mobility, or survey recall effects rather than a stable generational cultural divide.

observations.period: 2024 cultural-outings barometer; income and territorial gradients

denominator.unit: online survey respondents aged 15 years and above living in France

museum_low_income.unit: percent of low-income people visiting a museum or exhibition

museum_high_income.unit: percent of high-income people visiting a museum or exhibition

theatre_low_income.unit: percent of low-income people attending theatre

theatre_high_income.unit: percent of high-income people attending theatre

cinema_large_urban.unit: percent of residents of large urban centres going to the cinema

cinema_rural.unit: percent of residents of rural areas with dispersed or very dispersed housing going to the cinema

library_income_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between high-income and low-income library participation

mechanism.value: Free or lower-cost institutions such as libraries show narrower income gradients than museums and theatre, while urban concentration remains visible for cinema and other outings

observations.method: Descriptive income and commune-density cross-tabulations from the 2024 CREDOC cultural-outings module; income categories and territorial categories are defined by the source publication.
observations.uncertainty: The evidence does not isolate ticket price, travel time, local supply, household composition, or cultural preference; income associations are not causal estimates.
observations.subgroup: Income groups and commune-density categories among people aged 15 years and above in France.
observations.counterinterpretation: The narrower library gap may reflect different use cases and school or work access rather than proof that price is the dominant mechanism for all cultural outings.

related_sources.claim: The Ministry of Culture publication page documents the 2024 cultural-outings barometer, its 3,000-person sample, and its relationship to the CREDOC Conditions de vie et aspirations survey.
The Ministry's 2025 culture statistics page provides the detailed 2024 cultural-outings summary and subgroup tables used for the education, income, age, and territorial comparisons.

boundary: This record adds France's official 2024 cultural-recovery evidence with persistent education, income, age, gender, and territorial gradients. It does not estimate causal price or time effects, online participation, individual welfare, or equal recovery across all groups; the underlying survey is an online self-report of 3,000 people.
